newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - secondary gains after data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - secondary gains after data.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices gained slightly in early Wednesday trading, after market-friendly data reassured investors on inflation.
"We're up about (one basis point), but there's not much trading," one market participant said.
The Labor Department said consumer prices in June rose just 0.1 percent overall, versus expectations for a 0.2 percent rise.
The figure was another piece of reassuring news for investors counting on inflation to remain tame, and again offered validation for the Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates steady.
Municipal gains were not yet as strong as the Treasury market's rise after the data. The government long bond was up 16/32 at 101-17/32, pushing the yield down to 6.51 percent.

In other data releases, the Federal Reserve said June industrial production rose 0.3 percent and capacity utilization was unchanged at 83.5 percent. Economists had expected a 0.2 percent rise in output and capacity utilization of 83.6 percent.
Analysts said the Fed data had little impact on the market.
In early Wednesday pricings, Bear Stearns & Co. said it tentatively priced $47 million Methodist Health Systems, Tenn., bonds at a top yield of 5.35 percent in 2015.
A total of $562 billion in 23 sales were expected to sell Wednesday, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $418 million in nine sales, with a $132 million United Nations Development, N.Y., offering through Goldman, Sachs & Co., topping the list.
On the competitive side, 14 sales totaling $144 million are scheduled. A $41 million Texas Public Faclities Authority offering at 1130 EDT is the largest.
The Standard and Poor's Corp Blue list, a gauge of the secondary market, rose to $1.056 billion from $955 million on Tuesday.
September municipal bond futures rose 17/32 to 120-1/32, while September Treasury bond futures gained 14/32 to 114-12/32. The MOB spread widened to 181 ticks from 178 at the close on Tuesday.
In the secondary market, bids on Bexar county, Texas, MBIA 5-1/4s of 2027 were down one basis point to 5.52 percent.
Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority FGIC 5.0s of 2027 were down two basis points to 5.37 percent.
